name: Obsidian Sync
tagline: Paid sync service for a local-first Markdown knowledge base

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Sync listed at $5/user/month monthly and $4/user/month annually.

verdictSummary: If you already accept local Markdown files, syncing folders across devices is a solved problem; the hard part is not the app, it is conflict-free convenience.
coreLoopDIY: Use a local Markdown folder, git/Syncthing/iCloud/Drive for sync, and optional scripts for backlinks/search.
requirements: Syncthing, Git, iCloud, Dropbox, or similar
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for no-drama sync across devices while keeping Obsidian's local-first model.

priorArt.name: Syncthing
priorArt.desc: Open-source continuous file synchronization that can replace much of Obsidian Sync for tec

notes: Very clean yes; lets the site distinguish app value from convenience subscription.
prompt:
Build me a personal replacement for Obsidian Sync (Paid sync service for a local-first Markdown knowledge base). Requirements:

- Core loop: Use a local Markdown folder, git/Syncthing/iCloud/Drive for sync, and optional scripts for backlinks/search.
- Needs: local Markdown folder.
- Needs: Syncthing, Git, iCloud, Dropbox, or similar.
- Needs: optional mobile file access.
- Keep it personal-scale: no accounts, no telemetry, secrets in .env, SQLite or
  flat files for storage. Local-first wherever possible.
- Clean minimal UI where one is needed; CLI is fine where one is not.
- Include a README with setup steps, required keys, and any OS permissions.

Honest scope: this covers the core loop only. You will not get: official mobile sync polish; conflict handling; version history UI.
